post_title: Bias cut
post_details: Hello dear Clo Users, does somebody know if it is possible to simulate with bias cut? For example for certain cuts such as tight-fitting skirts that become wide at the bottom (possible through diagonal grain direction, which makes the fabric wrap around the body). I thought it might be possible by adjusting the physical properties (Details), however my problem is that I don't know exactly what feature i should adjust and at which value. I would be very grateful for suggestions. Best Regards Oganesya

comments.comment_body: Hi 902239802823 Yes, you can simulate bias in clo. It can be done two ways. 1) Select the pattern piece you want to change to Bias in either 2D or 3D. Then go to the Property Editor and scroll down to Fabric &gt Grain Direction &gt input the angle you wish to change it to. (most likely 45) 2) Start with the Edit Texture Tool (both 2D or 3D will work). Select the pattern piece you want to change to Bias in either 2D or 3D. The grain line arrow will appear and you can manually rotate the arrow at the top or bottom Hope this helps!

post_title: RGB Color Map (Suggestion)
post_details: Hiya, I have a suggestion for a feature I would love to see added to the CLO program. This is to mainly do with fabrics, but could no doubt be useful across the program as a whole. I would love to see an option for there to be an RGB map which means we can change certain texture area's colors. I've seen this method used in the workings of the game 'The Sims 3' in which an RGB (sometimes RGBK) map is used. An RGBK map reads each colorway from a seperate image file (comprised of areas of red, green, blue and black (key)) and assigns an editable color value to each one (allowing up to 4 editable colors). This would give us CLO users the potential of 4 editable color lines instead of fabrics etc only being able to be edited in one whole color. This would be useful for someone like myself who works a lot with textures such as injects, marls and tie dyes which so far can only be changed externally if it involves a white/light base but darker accent color. Below are a couple of examples of what an RGB map would look like (I've done just red and blue for now for quickness): These are examples of a tie dye and an inject jersey. Doing this would also mean we could have multiple colorways of these textured fabrics in one file and also look more realistic for allowing us to recolor just a standard jersey texture but with different colors. I hope this all makes sense and potentially some other used would agree with me in finding this helpful!

comments.comment_body: Hi 6341421371417, Thanks for the suggestion. Much appreciated. We recently released "Color Switch" feature, where you can input the total number of colors of your texture and change them individually. You can find it in the "Texture Editor". Best,

post_title: Reversed Normal Maps on Topstitch & Seams
post_details: Hiya, I'm having an issue with the normal maps of topstitching and seams when rendering. In the 3D view they are showing as intended: However when rendered, they are appearing as reversed: Any advice will be greatly appreciated!

comments.comment_body: Hi 6341421371417, Thanks for reaching out. It seems like the seam lines are accentuated due to the light settings in rendering. You can also adjust the intensity of the normal map applied on sewing line. With "Edit Sewing B" tool, click on the sewing line and adjust the "3D Seamline" in the Property Editor. Hope it helps. Best,

Hiya, Thank you for your reply. A further issue is that this has only happened with this project - all of my other project renders have been fine and use the same render settings across them all? The normal reversing doesn't happen to the front of the garment render for the first custom view, but after that for all other custom views this reversing happens? Many thanks,

brandalliance, the thing about normals, is they are just shading, not geometry. As such it's always possible for the eye to see them in reverse--is it popping out or sinking in? Looking at your hood in the 3d quality render, I see along the top right corner of the center panel seam there's a strong dark/light shadow. My eye reads that as a ditch, where light is some how reaching the right side, and shadowing the left (my eye presumes the light source is in the upper right). In your final render, there's the same strong shading configuration along that section of seam, dark on the left/light on the right. But this time my eye reads it as a hill, where the right side is catching light and blocking light on the back (light from the right?). Neither perception is "correct", they are both just an optical illusion applied to a flat object. I think the maps are applied consistently in both scenes. I agree if you adjust the intensity, the eye may be less drawn to the seams, and let other clues about the lighting set the perception.

post_title: bad quality renders
post_details: hi, no matter what i seem to do my renders look terrible. ive kept playing with different settings and ligthts, same result. :`( can someone help me? thank you

comments.comment_body: Hello! You are rendering a large size with really high quality settings, so if you want it to render without noise, you will need to let it run a lot longer than the time you have set. What is the image for? Does it need to be that size? (at the moment its about 5000 x 6000 pixels). If you change that so the resolution is halved (ie same size at 300dpi) it will take probably about a quarter of the time (or for a set period of time, much better quality). Try running the render overnight with nothing else running on your computer if you really want that size, but I dont think the noise will clear up well with those quality settings. I would recommend reducing the resolution and turning the quality down a few notches. You can always get rid of a little noise afterwards in an image editor. I find Clo can produce some lovely images (its got a good render engine based on VRay) but I tend to export models to another 3D program if I want more control or speed for rendering. Rendering is quite a hard thing for computers to do so it definitely helps if you have a fast computer/more RAM/better graphics card etc. If you dont have access to these you will have to turn down the settings a bit or let it take more time (or use a few tricks like upscaling afterwards). Adam
If you can send me the file, I can make a quick video showing you what I would do to render this out nicely. Adam

post_title: what happend after style line editing?
post_details: May I ask does the CLO3D re-simulate the garment based on the new pattern right after moving style line? If so, then why pressing the simulation button again will give us different results? If not, then why does the 3D garment change after moving style line? Thank you.

comments.comment_body: It's similar to making edits in the 2D window. The mesh changes immediately and the 3D window shows that, but the ways the sewing relations and fabric physics pull those pieces doesn't happen until you simulate. So best practice is alternating: small edit, simulate, small edit, simulate...

Hi jpreo, Thank you very much for your kind reply. May I further ask do you know does the CLO3D do a part simulation (only simulate the corresponded 3D part of the edited 2D pattern) to do 'making edits in the 2D window. The mesh changes immediately and the 3D window shows that'? Best, Ann

When you make a change to your pattern in 2D you will immediately see the change in the 3D window, but CLO will not recalculate the of the garment till you turn on simulation. Once you turn on Simulation it will recalculate the drape of everything in the window and not just what you changed.
Thank you very much for your help. My question is how does the system make that immediate change in 3D? Best, Ann

It will follow the current direction of how the garment is hanging/draping. Which is why sometimes the pattern piece might cut into the avatar, but as soon as you simulate the garment will adjust to drape properly. See below images. 1) The Tee as is 2)The Tee with the hem lengthened. In 3D it extents how it was previously draped. Going straight down in the middle, but flaring out at the sides where it previously flared at the avatars hips 3) Simulation turned on and adjusted
Thank you very much for your kind help and explanation. Get your point! Best, Ann

post_title: 3D state lost after using the 2D reset pattern along grainline
post_details: There's a problem with the new reset along grain direction tool, under Transform Pattern: Rotate. The issue is after a pattern has been reset along the grain in the 2D window, it's 3D state seems to be destroyed and will reset as soon as there's an update like an edit to the same pattern, or really anything that causes an update bar (even an edit to another pattern). I haven't seen this behavior before. To recreate: Create a square and simulate so it has a 3D state (or place with curvature on an arrangement point) Rotate the pattern piece in the 2D window by some non zero angle Reset the pattern along grainline in the 2D window Make a small edit to the pattern, like moving a vertex In the 3D window the square will reset to a plank of some sort depending on collisions. Pressing undo will not restore the lost configuration. The only option is simulate or reset 2D. Compare to a similar edit after one of the other pattern rotations. In that case the 3D state updates a will need to simulate, but doesn't reset to a plank. The same thing happens if the pattern has been placed with an arrangement point but not simulated. If the pattern is already on grain and reset along grain has no effect, then there is no issue. If the pattern is in an un-simulated state, already a plank, nothing happens. It has nothing to do with pattern symmetry, e.g. it was noted that "reset pattern" doesn't work on both symmetric patterns unless both are selected. Other 2d rotation tools work simultaneously. (Personally I like that it's now possible to reset only one.) Setup: After using Rotate: reset along grain direction Editing the pattern in 2D is a quick way to trigger the behavior, but once the tool has been used, I believe it will reset shortly during work even without further edits to that pattern piece

comments.comment_body: For comparison, typically a small edit does not reset the pattern, just causes a local adjustment to the pattern shape in the 3D window
